stem.text: The function f is differentiable for all real numbers, and selected values of f are given in the table. Must there be a value c, with \( 3 < c < 9 \), for which \( f(c) = -5 \)? Justify your answer.

answer_key.label: Yes. Since f is differentiable, it is continuous on \( [3, 9] \), and \( f(3) = -9 < -5 < f(9) = 3 \), so the Intermediate Value Theorem gives at least one such c.

worked_solution.text: Because f is differentiable, f is continuous, in particular on \( [3, 9] \).
From the table, \( f(3) = -9 < -5 < f(9) = 3 \), so -5 lies between the values of f at the ends of \( [3, 9] \).
By the Intermediate Value Theorem there is at least one c with \( 3 < c < 9 \) and \( f(c) = -5 \). So yes, such a c must exist.

options.label: Yes. The Intermediate Value Theorem needs no hypothesis beyond \( f(3) = -9 < -5 < f(9) = 3 \), so it gives at least one such c.
options.derivation: the theorem applied with the continuity hypothesis never established
